$comment: Native realtime conversation state machine (P3-U3 reducer contract, rules 1-8). Input: the 12 unified events of realtime-events.v1 (same keys as its mapCases.expected; itemId may be null and is never used for matching) plus local inputs mute / unmute / tapOrb / playbackDrained / playbackProgress{itemId, playedMs} / tick{ms} / end / systemInterruption / failed{code} / screenReaderSpeaking{speaking} / planChanged / gateOpened / wake. Each case replays steps from the initial state; every step locks the statusKey after the input and the ordered effects it emits. scripts/voice-contracts-check.mjs recomputes every expected with scripts/lib/realtime-conversation.mjs; each client implements the same reducer and replays this fixture. displayCases lock the rendered user caption and revealed assistant text (E-450 / E-451), revealCases the reveal function alone. Failure categories, picker, capability, migration and lifecycle: realtime-model.v1.json.

state: 1. State: phase connecting | listening | thinking | speaking | ended; muted; userSpeaking; drainPending; turn {userPending, userText, assistantStarted, assistantDone, assistantText, heldMs, userAfterReply, awaitingDrain, frozenPlayedMs, audioSamples, sampleRateHz, played}; idleMs; thinkingMs; earconDone; dormant; reopenAwaitingProgress; screenReaderSpeaking. Initial phase is connecting with everything else false / empty / 0, frozenPlayedMs null and played an empty map (itemId, null as "", → played ms), audioItems empty (item keys that delivered audio this turn).
statusKey: ended → null; connecting → thinking; listening while muted → muted; otherwise the phase. Muted does not override thinking or speaking.
Inputs with an unknown type change nothing (idleMs included) and emit nothing. After ended every input is ignored.

stageLine (E-525): the one line of the voice stage. ended → null; userCaption non-null → {kind user, text}; phase speaking with a non-empty assistantShown → {kind assistant, text}; otherwise {kind status, statusKey}. displayCases lock it with userCaption and assistantShown.
transitions: ready → listening only from connecting; a later ready (reconnect) changes nothing.

userSpeechStarted → listening, userSpeaking = true, userPending = true, thinkingMs = 0, earconDone = false. While speaking it first emits interruptPlayback and freezes the reveal (see persistence). When no utterance was pending, userText is cleared first, so an earlier final text is never shown as this utterance's caption or written as its draft. A held reply, or a finished reply still waiting for playback (awaitingDrain), is released (persisted) before the new utterance starts; if the current reply has started but is not done, the utterance is marked userAfterReply (it belongs to the next turn).
userSpeechStopped → thinking from any live phase, userSpeaking = false, thinkingMs = 0.

assistantAudio → speaking, marks the reply started, adds floor(decoded base64 bytes / 2) samples (PCM16 mono) to audioSamples, sampleRateHz = the event's rate (one output rate per turn) and records its item key (null as "") in audioItems; assistantTranscript stores the cumulative assistant text and marks the reply started. playbackProgress {itemId, playedMs} (local, from the player, cumulative per item): playedMs is floored to an integer; it is ignored when negative or not finite, when the phase is not speaking, when the item key is not in audioItems (a late report from the previous reply never leaks into this one) or once the reveal is frozen; otherwise the item stores max(previous, playedMs). It does not reset idleMs. None of these change anything else.

assistantTurnDone: while speaking stays speaking with drainPending = true, otherwise → listening. playbackDrained: when speaking with drainPending → listening; in any phase it then releases a reply waiting for playback (awaitingDrain; e.g. a userSpeechStopped without a start already moved to thinking); otherwise it changes nothing (more audio may follow).

interrupted → freezes the reveal, → listening (drainPending cleared) and releases a reply waiting for playback. tapOrb only while speaking: interruptPlayback, freeze, → listening, release; in every other phase it is a no-op (it does not unmute).

goAway / resumable change nothing in this reducer (reconnect and resumption belong to the session layer) but still reset idleMs. The unified error event is non-fatal (realtime-events.v1: the connection close decides fatality): it changes nothing and emits nothing, only resets idleMs; the conversation continues.

planChanged (local; at a turn boundary the host replans off the main thread with currentSessionId = the open session and sends this when the new fingerprint differs from the open session’s, per realtime-session.v1): only in phase listening, not dormant, not userSpeaking and with no turn in progress (no userPending, no assistantStarted) → drainPending = false, turn cleared, phase connecting (statusKey thinking), emit reopen; the host reopens from the new plan and sends ready. Otherwise ignored; the host compares again at the next turn boundary.
persistence: userTranscript stores text in userText. Non-final sets userPending = true (Gemini sends no speech-start signal). Final sets userPending = false and emits persist {role: user, text: trimmed} unless echoUnits(text) is empty (blank or punctuation / separators only, same separator set as voice-conversation.v1 isEcho).

Reveal (E-451): revealPrefix(text, playedMs, audioSamples, sampleRateHz): playedMs is floored, negative counts as 0; "" when there is no audio or no text; the whole text when playedMs >= floor(audioSamples * 1000 / sampleRateHz) (everything received has played); otherwise k = floor(n * playedMs * sampleRateHz / (audioSamples * 1000)) code points of the received text (n = code points; integer arithmetic, the product needs 64 bits), the whole text when k >= n. k never stops before a combining mark (\p{M}) or ZWJ and otherwise backs off to a boundary: start, whitespace on either side, or an unspaced-script character (CJK, kana, hangul, Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar, fullwidth forms) on either side. Whitespace is exactly the ECMAScript \s set (TAB LF VT FF CR SPACE U+00A0 U+1680 U+2000..U+200A U+2028 U+2029 U+202F U+205F U+3000 U+FEFF; Kotlin isWhitespace misses U+00A0), the same set trims the result and every trimmed text in this contract. Freezing records frozenPlayedMs = the sum of played ms once per reply (only after the reply started); text that still arrives afterwards (often only with assistantTurnDone) is revealed at the frozen played time. The persisted assistant text is the trimmed revealPrefix at frozenPlayedMs when frozen, otherwise the full text; a reply frozen before any audio (text only, or nothing played) persists nothing.

assistantTurnDone text = event.text when it is non-blank after trim, otherwise the latest assistantTranscript (null and "" both fall back). While speaking and not frozen the reply waits for playback (awaitingDrain = true, nothing written yet, E-451). Otherwise hold-or-persist: if userPending and the utterance is not userAfterReply, a reply whose persisted text would be non-blank is held (heldMs = 0) and a blank one clears the reply half of the turn (assistant fields and the freeze reset, userPending / userText kept) so nothing carries into the next reply; else persist {role: assistant, text} immediately (blank writes nothing). Releasing a reply that waited for playback follows the same hold-or-persist rule.

A held reply is released by the user final (persist user first, then assistant), by tick when heldMs reaches lateUserTranscriptMs (assistant only; a later user final is then persisted on its own), by the next userSpeechStarted, or by the end sequence.

Barge-in: if the userAfterReply utterance goes final before the interrupted reply is written, the reply is frozen (if not yet) and persisted first with its prefix, then the user text; when its assistantTurnDone had not arrived yet, that later assistantTurnDone writes nothing (replyFlushed); when it had arrived (the reply was waiting for playback) nothing is skipped. If the reply finishes first it is persisted immediately and the utterance (pending flag and text) carries over to the next turn.
After a reply is written the turn is cleared, except the userPending / userText of a userAfterReply utterance.
mute: mute (when not muted): muted = true; if userSpeaking emit sendSilence {ms: muteSilenceMs} first, then setUplink {on: false}. unmute (when muted): muted = false, setUplink {on: true}. Repeated mute / unmute emit nothing.

sessionExpired (local; the host sends it when the transport reports the provider closed the session as expired, Gemini close 1008): ignored while dormant; otherwise reopenAwaitingProgress is checked first, then muted (same order as realtime-model afterDrop: reopenedWithoutProgress before muted, E-611 / E-630). While muted, not dormant and reopenAwaitingProgress false → persist a held assistant reply (a reply waiting for playback is frozen first and persists its revealed prefix), then dormant = true, phase listening, turn cleared, no effects (the call stays open, statusKey muted, idle does not count while muted). Ignored while dormant. unmute while dormant → dormant = false, reopenAwaitingProgress = true, phase connecting, emit reopen then setUplink {on: true}; the host opens a new session from the text history and sends ready when it is up. E-200 (咪咪 2026-10-20 option B).

wake (local; the host sends it when the user types while dormant, E-634 overriding E-613): only while dormant → dormant = false, reopenAwaitingProgress = true, phase connecting (statusKey thinking), emit reopen; muted, the uplink and screenReaderSpeaking are untouched (no setUplink), so the reopened session stays muted until the user unmutes. Not dormant (connecting, reopening, live, muted but not dormant) → ignored, no effects; a second wake while the reopen is connecting does not reopen again. Cases rt_dormant_wake_reopens_keeps_mute_typed_persists_once, rt_wake_not_dormant_noop, rt_dormant_wake_twice_reopens_once_then_expired_ends_error.

Not muted (and not dormant) with reopenAwaitingProgress false → persist a held assistant reply (a reply waiting for playback is frozen first and persists its revealed prefix), turn cleared, userSpeaking = false, drainPending = false, reopenAwaitingProgress = true, phase connecting (statusKey thinking), emit reopen (uplink gating unchanged, it stays on); the host reopens from the text history and sends ready, which goes connecting → listening. If reopenAwaitingProgress is true (muted or not) → showError {code: "unknown"} then end with reason error (no reopen loop; while muted too, so a mute after an unprogressed reopen cannot cycle dormant → reopen). reopenAwaitingProgress is cleared by userTranscript, assistantAudio, assistantTranscript or assistantTurnDone; ready is not progress. E-203.

screenReaderSpeaking{speaking} (local; the host sends it when the platform screen reader starts / finishes announcing): screenReaderSpeaking = speaking. Uplink is on only when not muted and the screen reader is not speaking; mute wins. speaking true while not muted → setUplink {on: false}; speaking false while not muted → setUplink {on: true}; while muted both emit nothing and muted / statusKey are unchanged. unmute while the screen reader is speaking clears muted but does not emit setUplink {on: true} (reopen still applies while dormant). Repeated values emit nothing.
timers: tick{ms} is the only clock. There is no periodic tick (E-222): after every reduce the host arms one one-shot timer for nextTickMs (cancelling the previous one; none when null); before dispatching any other input, and when that timer fires, it first dispatches tick{ms: monotonic time elapsed since the last tick or since the session became ready}. nextTickMs = min of (lateUserTranscriptMs - heldMs while a reply is held, thinkingEarconMs - thinkingMs while thinking and the earcon has not played, idleEndMs - idleMs while listening, not muted and not userSpeaking), clamped at 0; null when none applies or ended. A tick with ms <= 0 changes nothing, so the host never arms a timer for nextTickMs <= 0 (it would only spin). In this order: held reply heldMs += ms (release at lateUserTranscriptMs); while thinking thinkingMs += ms and the first time it reaches thinkingEarconMs emit earcon (once until the next userSpeechStarted); while listening, not muted and not userSpeaking idleMs += ms and at idleEndMs run the end sequence with reason idle.
Every input other than tick and playbackProgress resets idleMs to 0, including goAway, resumable, mute, unmute and no-op tapOrb.

playbackDrained comes from the player's own completion callback when the last queued buffer has played; the host never polls the player. When drainPending turns on and the player has already played everything (so no callback will follow), the host reads the player's state once at that moment and dispatches playbackDrained.

playbackProgress comes from the player at the cadence the host already redraws the reply bubble (at most every 100 ms while speaking, plus once right before the host dispatches userSpeechStarted, tapOrb, interrupted or end while speaking); it is never polled for the reducer alone.
end: end → reason user; systemInterruption and sessionEnded → reason system, except sessionEnded with reason max_duration or timeout, which emits showError {code: max_duration} and ends with reason error. Local failed {code} (sent by the host after classifying the failure with realtime-model.v1 failureCases) → emit showError {code} first, then reason error; a code outside the six categories becomes unknown. A session that expires again after a reopen without progress emits showError {code: unknown}. showError codes are always one of auth, quota, model_gone, max_duration, network, unknown.

End sequence, in order: a reply waiting for playback is frozen and becomes releasable; persist a held assistant reply (its frozen prefix when frozen); for reason user only, writeDraft {text: trimmed userText} when userPending and echoUnits(userText) is non-empty; close; ended {reason}. Then phase = ended, statusKey null. A reply still being generated (not done) is not persisted.
fixture: cases[]: {id, steps: [{input, expected: {statusKey, effects[], nextTickMs}}]}. Effects: persist {role, text}, interruptPlayback, sendSilence {ms}, setUplink {on}, earcon, showError {code}, writeDraft {text}, close, ended {reason}, reopen, disableBargeIn.

displayCases[]: {id, steps: [{input, expected: {userCaption, assistantShown}}]} replay the same reducer and lock what the host renders after each step. userCaption (E-450) = trimmed userText while userPending and echoUnits(userText) is non-empty, else null (no placeholder bubble; after the final the text is a message). assistantShown = revealPrefix at frozenPlayedMs when frozen; the full trimmed text when a reply is held or waited for playback without any audio; otherwise revealPrefix at the summed played ms; "" once the reply is persisted (it is then a message). No per-provider branch.
revealCases[]: {id, input: {text, playedMs, audioSamples, sampleRateHz}, expected: string} lock revealPrefix alone.
host: Home entry (no conversation yet): on the first assistantAudio, assistant transcript or user transcript event of the session, the host creates the chat and moves to the chat page on the main thread BEFORE it reduces that event and publishes the status, so the home bar never shows speaking (voice-conversation pageReachableStatusKeys.home). Later persist effects write into that conversation in effect order (user before assistant per rules.persistence). Event order does not matter: an assistant reply that arrives before any user transcript still lands on the chat page.
Only the home entry does this. A chat-page entry (draft or existing conversation) never creates through this path and never deletes.
The host tries to create once per session. If creation fails it ends the session with the same error the home cascade first send uses, so the home bar never reaches speaking.

A home session deletes the conversation it created only when all hold: it created it, it persisted nothing into it, and the store still has no message in it (checked and deleted in one transaction, not counted as a user delete). Creation and the handoff are not cancellable halfway: an end during creation still records the created id so the empty check runs. The page holding that conversation is left (only when it is still the current page) before or atomically with the delete, so no send can target a conversation being deleted: iOS removes it from memory and dismisses in one main-actor turn, then deletes in the store; Android leaves the page, then deletes in one transaction. A delete skipped because the store has messages navigates no further.

One user turn, one user message: every inputTranscription fragment of one user turn (until that turn ends at turnComplete; a provider item id, when present, groups fragments the same way) accumulates into one text and is persisted once at the turn boundary. Fragments are never persisted one by one, and two real turns are never merged after the fact.
The event that triggers home creation (often the first user fragment) is not lost: it is reduced only after creation finished, in arrival order, with every later event queued behind it.

Replay: recordings/*.v1.json (gemini-live-home-two-turn with its variants, gemini-live-barge-in) hold real provider server messages; both ends replay them in order through the production mapper, reducer and sink and must produce expectedMessages exactly (order, count, text). The replay models an ideal player: after each assistantAudio it dispatches playbackProgress with all audio received so far for that item, and right after an assistantTurnDone received while speaking it dispatches playbackDrained. Recordings store audio as {audioBytes: N} placeholders; the replay feeds the reducer an assistantAudio whose base64 decodes to N bytes (or the same sample count) so the reveal ratio is exact.
end is synchronous for the UI: active turns false and the bar hides in the same call; audio teardown finishes in the background and never blocks navigation.

Typed text (typing mode, E-589 / E-524): at the moment it is actually sent on a ready connection the host reduces userSpeechStarted, userSpeechStopped and userTranscript final for it (one persist), then sends the text; while connecting or reopening it is queued without reducing; while dormant it is queued and the host reduces wake (reopen, mute kept, E-634 / E-524). A reopen history never contains queued text and the model never receives it twice: on the new connection's ready the queue is reduced (one persist each) and sent in order. Cases rt_typed_text_idle_persists_once and rt_typed_text_while_speaking_barges_in.
uplinkGate: Speaker route only: from the frame the host starts rendering assistant audio (playbackStartFrame) until postPlaybackGuardMs (voice-conversation constants) after playback truly ended, uplink frames are held and not sent; headphones / bluetooth never hold (uplinkGateCases expected by scripts/lib/realtime-conversation.mjs uplinkGate).

The voiced decision is the cascade runVad on 20 ms post-AEC capture dBFS (same frame dB the cascade VAD uses), with resetVad at playbackStartFrame (drops only the open utterance and voiced run; the E-415 follow-up reference survives, so a barge-in shortly after the user's own previous utterance is not held by the background level that utterance raised, E-708, rt_gate_model_barge_in_soon_after_user_sentence_opens): barge-in grace bargeInGraceMs, barge-in needs bargeInMinSpeechMs continuous voice, the guard window needs postPlaybackGuardMinSpeechMs. Model mode (E-420): when the local speech model (Silero, 16 kHz) is ready the host attaches its latest speech probability to every gate frame ({db, prob}; runVad model mode incl. the E-376 background-level gate), so loud but non-speech residual echo (AEC degraded mid-session) stays held while a real barge-in with high prob opens; the mode is fixed by the first gate frame (prob present = model mode). Speech-like residual echo (high prob, level above the background gate) still opens after grace (rt_gate_model_speechlike_echo_opens_after_grace) and is bounded by the false barge-in downgrade.

Model source (E-420): the host starts loading the model when the session opens and, after the transport is ready and before capture starts, waits until at most 500 ms after session open (same budget as the cascade, E-375; never delays connecting); not ready, load error, or the session ending first = energy mode for the whole session and a late model is closed. The model is fed 16 kHz audio derived from the capture (any resample path; a resampler failure counts as an inference failure) continuously from capture start, its state is never reset at playback start (warm state; fresh state over-reads babble, E-376), and each 20 ms frame carries the latest probability after that frame was fed (0 before the first 512-sample chunk). The model is closed when the session ends. An inference failure mid-session (frame prob null) hands the rest of the session to a fresh energy VAD instance (E-375); in-progress voice is dropped; it never returns to model mode.

Echo reference (F2c, E-430): in model mode the host also attaches to every gate frame the downlink reference level ref = dBFS of the assistant PCM block (20 ms, the one being rendered at the player head position when the capture frame is gated; null = nothing rendering), frames [db, n, prob, ref] in uplinkGateCases. Both series are clamped to [echoRefFloorDb, 0] (null = floor). Delay d* = the lag 0..echoRefMaxDelayMs with the highest Pearson correlation between the last echoRefDelayWindowMs of capture dB and the lagged reference (ties: smaller lag; a constant window is unusable; the whole window must lie in frames already seen). A frame in [playbackStartFrame, guard end) is echo when the d* long-window correlation is >= echoRefMinDelayCorrelation and, on d*, the correlation over the last echoRefWindowMs is >= echoRefMinCorrelation (the long-window floor keeps a barge-in after the AEC fully cancelled the echo from looking like echo, rt_gate_echo_ref_speech_after_suppressed_echo_opens) and its capture dB <= aligned reference + gain + echoRefBargeInMarginDb (gain = lower median of capture minus reference over that short window where the reference is above the floor; none = not echo). An echo frame is fed to the VAD with prob 0 (its dB still feeds the floor / background); anything that cannot be judged is not echo. Energy mode and frames after an inference failure ignore ref. Barge-in louder than the predicted echo by the margin, or uncorrelated with it, still opens (rt_gate_echo_ref_*). rt_gate_echo_ref_samsung_barge_in_opens is a real Samsung trace slice (barge-in injected after AEC, onset at frame 120) that a 0.6 long-window floor held for 18 frames (E-433). Onset backtrack (E-434, same idea as E-413): when frames carry ref and the gate opens on speech, the flush start moves back to (first frame of the earliest run of >= vadModelOnsetMinRunFrames frames with post-echo-reference prob >= vadModelStartProb and db >= vadAbsoluteMinDb, searched from max(playbackStartFrame + bargeInGraceMs, run start - vadModelOnsetBacktrackMs) up to the run start) - vadPrerollMs, never before playbackStartFrame; so a barge-in whose first syllable is shorter than bargeInMinSpeechMs is not clipped (rt_gate_echo_ref_samsung_split_onset_backtracks, real Samsung slice, onset at frame 120).

Open on speech: at the detecting frame send the held frames from max(playbackStartFrame, runVad prerollFrame) in order, then stream live; frames before that are dropped (not replaced by silence). Open at guard end: send the last vadPrerollMs of held frames, then stream live. Once open, the gate stays open until the next playback start re-arms it.

Playback end = the host true end (iOS RealtimePlaybackDrain drained after dataPlayedBack, Android onDrained marker) or a local stopPlayback (interrupt / tap orb). A new playback start while held or in the guard window starts a new cycle.

Route is sampled when a playback cycle starts: only a speaker route arms that cycle (a route change mid-cycle takes effect at the next cycle). Mute and screen-reader setUplink(off) take precedence: an open gate still sends nothing while the uplink is off.

On an open with openReason speech the host feeds gateOpened to the reducer. The next final userTranscript is a false barge-in when it is empty after echoUnits or isEcho against the reply being played and the last persisted reply; at falseBargeInsPerSession the reducer emits disableBargeIn once and the host sets bargeIn=false on the gate for the rest of the session (tap orb still interrupts); while speaking after that, statusKey is speakingTapToInterrupt (same key and copy as the cascade).

Server turn detection config is unchanged (OpenAI semantic_vad, xAI server_vad, Gemini default automatic activity detection): with the gate the server never hears held echo, and an opened barge-in reaches it with preroll so its own userSpeechStarted / interrupted drives the existing interrupt path.
